([[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 19 | draft_team = [[New York Knicks]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Greensboro Swarm]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = [[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years4 = {{nbay|2023|end}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team5 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | years6 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team6 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years7 = 2025–present | team7 = [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] | highlights = * [[Big 12]] Sixth Man of the Year (2021) }} '''Kai Martinez Jones''' (born January 19, 2001) is a Bahamian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He previously played in the NBA for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] and [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Nassau, Bahamas]], Jones moved to the United States when he was 11 years old. After his sophomore year in high school, he returned to his home country hoping to pursue a career as a [[long jump]]er. At age 15, Jones played organized basketball for his first time, being drawn to the sport after having a growth spurt.{{cite web|first=Evan|last=Daniels|title=Kai Jones shows well at Global Academy, as interest picks up|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Kai-Jones-shows-well-at-Global-Academy-as-college-interest-picks-up-118810166/|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=June 5, 2018|access-date=September 15, 2019}} ==High school career== In the summer of 2017, Jones took part in a [[Basketball Without Borders]] Americas camp held by the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in Nassau.{{cite web|title=BWB Americas come to an end in The Bahamas|url=https://thenassauguardian.com/2017/07/11/bwb-americas-come-to-an-end-in-the-bahamas/|work=[[The Nassau Guardian]]|date=July 11, 2017|access-date=September 15, 2019}}{{Dead link|date=February 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=Scouting the most interesting draft prospects at the NBA Global Camp|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23651773|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=June 7, 2018|access-date=September 15, 2019}} That year, he worked out with and took advice from top high school recruit [[Deandre Ayton]] in their hometown of Nassau. As a result, Jones was inspired to play basketball in the United States.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=McMullen|title=Texas lands Bahamian big man Kai Jones, who worked out with Deandre Ayton|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/10/15/kai-jones-to-texas/|website=ZagsBlog.com|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=September 14, 2019}} For the 2017–18 season, he enrolled at [[Orlando Christian Prep]] in [[Orlando, Florida]], as a high school senior. He was teammates with five-star recruits [[Nassir Little]] and C. J. Walker and helped win the [[Florida High School Athletic Association]] (FHSAA) Class 3A state championship.{{cite web|first=Jake|last=Perper|title=2019 F Kai Jones talks OCP state title, recruitment and more|url=https://www.prephoops.com/2018/06/2019-f-kai-jones-talks-ocp-state-title-recruitment-and-more/|website=PrepHoops.com|date=June 5, 2018|access-date=September 14, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Kemp|title=Canterbury falls in Class 3A state championship game|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/06/boys-basketball-canterbury-falls-class-3-championship-game/399491002/|work=[[The News-Press]]|date=March 7, 2018|access-date=September 14, 2019}} In high school, Jones woke up at 4:45 a.m. every day to train and played basketball after school.{{cite web|first=Renaldo|last=Dorsett|title=Kai Jones Commits To The University Of Texas Longhorns|url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2018/oct/16/kai-jones-commits-university-texas-longhorns/|work=The Tribune|date=October 16, 2018|access-date=September 15, 2019}} At the same time, he saw academic success, graduating with a 4.2 [[Grading in education|grade point average]] and [[Latin honors|summa cum laude]] honors. In the summer of 2018, Jones attended the NBA Global Camp in [[Treviso]], Italy. Following his senior year, he played a [[postgraduate season]] at [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]].{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Snow|title=Kai Jones shows major potential and is ready to make impact|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Top-60-prospect-Kai-Jones-is-ready-to-make-an-impact-for-Shaka-Smart-at-Texas-127221347/|work=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]|date=January 2, 2019|access-date=September 15, 2019}} On February 4, 2019, Jones was named to the National Prep Invitational all-tournament team.{{cite web|first=Renaldo|last=Dorsett|title=Jones Named In Tournament Team|url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2019/feb/06/jones-named-tournament-team/|work=The Tribune|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=September 15, 2019}} In March, he helped Brewster Academy win the USA National Prep Championship.{{cite web|first=Simba|last=French|title=Jones, Brewster Academy win National Prep Championships|url=https://thenassauguardian.com/2019/03/12/jones-brewster-academy-win-national-prep-championships/|work=[[The Nassau Guardian]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=September 15, 2019}}{{Dead link|date=February 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ===Recruiting=== On October 15, 2018, Jones committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. He chose to join the Longhorns over offers from several other [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{cite web|first=EJ|last=Holland|title=Four-star big man Kai Jones commits to Texas|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2018/10/16/four-star-big-man-kai-jones-commits-to-texas/|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=September 15, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Kai Jones | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Nassau, Bahamas]] | highschool = [[Brewster Academy]] (NH) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = October 15, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 88 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Texas 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Texas Longhorns Recruiting Class | rivals school = texas | scout s = | espn schoolid = 251 | 247 overall = 49 | rivals overall = 59 | espn overall = 53 | accessdate = September 15, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Coach [[Shaka Smart]] said that Jones had the best work ethic of any big man he coached. Despite this, Jones struggled to get playing time early in his freshman season. He gradually saw more playing time as the season progressed, finishing with eight points on 4–5 shooting from the field in just 10 minutes of the Longhorns' 73–71 win over [[McNeese State Cowboys men's basketball|McNeese State]] on November 30.{{cite news|first=Renaldo|last=Dorsett|title=Kai Jones Wants More Playing Time With Texas Longhorns|url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2019/dec/16/kai-jones-wants-more-playing-time-texas-longhorns/|work=Bahamas Tribune|date=December 16, 2019|access-date=January 15, 2020}} As a freshman, Jones averaged 3.6 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.{{cite news|first=Brian|last=Davis|title=Big 12 tournament men's preview: No. 4 seed Texas vs. No. 5 seed Texas Tech|url=https://www.hookem.com/2020/03/11/big-12-tournament-mens-preview-no-4-seed-texas-vs-no-5-seed-texas-tech/|work=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|date=March 11, 2020|access-date=April 10, 2020}} On January 26, 2021, he registered his first [[double-double]], with 15 points and 10 rebounds in an 80–79 loss to [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{cite web|first=Renaldo|last=Dorsett|title=Kai Jones posts his first double double in NCAA|url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2021/jan/28/kai-jones-posts-his-first-double-double-ncaa/|work=The Tribune|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=July 22, 2021}} Jones was named [[Big 12]] Sixth Man of the Year and to the All-Big 12 honorable mention.{{cite web|first=Roger|last=Wallace|title=Longhorns' Kai Jones named Big 12 Sixth Man of the Year|url=https://www.kxan.com/sports/longhorns-kai-jones-named-big-12-sixth-man-of-the-year/|work=[[KXAN-TV]]|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=July 22, 2021|archive-date=July 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210722224216/https://www.kxan.com/sports/longhorns-kai-jones-named-big-12-sixth-man-of-the-year/|url-status=dead}} As a sophomore, he averaged 8.8 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. On March 24, 2021, Jones declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite magazine|first=Madeline|last=Coleman|title=Texas Forward Kai Jones Declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/03/24/kai-jones-texas-declares-nba-draft|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 24, 2021|access-date=July 22, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets (2021–2023)=== Jones was selected with the 19th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]] and immediately traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Hornets acquire No. 19 pick in trade with Knicks|url=https://www.nba.com/news/knicks-trade-19th-pick-to-hornets-kai-jones|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=July 30, 2021}} On August 3, he officially signed with the Hornets.{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign James Bouknight and Kai Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-james-bouknight-and-kai-jones|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} On September 30, 2023, the Hornets announced that Jones would not participate in training camp and offered no timetable for his return to the team.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Statement Regarding Kai Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-statement-regarding-kai-jones|website=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2023|access-date=October 15, 2023}} The decision came after Jones displayed bizarre behavior on social media which included criticism of his teammates, incoherent speech, and declarations of being the greatest basketball player of all time.{{cite web|first=Yoko Nicole|last=Villarin|title=Charlotte Hornets Cuts Ties With Kai Jones After Public Trade Request|url=https://theindependent.sg/charlotte-hornets-cuts-ties-with-kai-jones-after-public-trade-request-sportsry/|work=The Independent Singapore|date=October 17, 2023|access-date=October 17, 2023}} On October 9, 2023, Jones publicly requested a trade on [[Twitter|X]]{{cite magazine|first=Schuyler|last=Callihan|title=Kai Jones Announces He Has Requested a Trade|url=https://www.si.com/nba/hornets/news/kai-jones-announces-he-has-requested-a-trade|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=October 9, 2023|access-date=October 9, 2023}} and two days later, he was waived by the Hornets.{{cite news|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Kai Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-kai-jones|website=NBA.com|date=October 11, 2023|access-date=October 11, 2023}} No team claimed his waiver, making him a free agent. He averaged 2.7 points in 9.1 minutes per game during his two seasons with the Hornets. ===Delaware Blue Coats (2024)=== On March 15, 2024, Jones signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Kai Jones to a 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-kai-jones|website=NBA.com|date=March 15, 2024|access-date=March 15, 2024}} However, he only played for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], Philadelphia's [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate.{{cite web|title=76ers' Kai Jones: Headed to G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-kai-jones-headed-to-g-league/|website=CBSSports.com|date=March 15, 2024|access-date=March 25, 2024}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2024–2025)=== On April 14, 2024, Jones signed for the rest of the season with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite tweet|author=LA Clippers|title=Welcome to #ClipperNation, Kai Jones!|number=1779560159548936224|user=LAClippers|date=April 14, 2024|access-date=April 14, 2024}} On July 9, he re-signed with the Clippers{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Clippers Sign Kai Jones To Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/clippers-to-sign-kai-jones-to-non-guaranteed-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=August 27, 2024}} and on October 19, his deal converted into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|first=Tristan|last=Tucker|title=Clippers Convert Kai Jones To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/clippers-converting-kai-jones-to-two-way-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} On March 1, 2025, the Clippers waived Jones.{{cite web | last=Esnaashari | first=Farbod | title=Breaking: LA Clippers Release Multiple Players After Lakers Game | website=Los Angeles Clippers On SI | date=2025-03-01 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/clippers/onsi/news/breaking-la-clippers-release-multiple-players-after-lakers-game-01jn9jrxw304 | access-date=2025-12-08}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2025)=== On March 2, 2025, Jones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]],{{cite web|title=With Mavericks’ new center, an old weapon may resurface|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-kai-jones/|website=mavs.com|date=March 3, 2025|access-date=March 3, 2025}}{{cite web|title=Mavericks Sign Kai Jones To Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-kai-jones-to-two-way-contract|website=gleague.nba.com|date=March 3, 2025|access-date=March 3, 2025}} and on March 3, he made his debut in Dallas, coming off the bench in a 122–98 loss over the [[Sacramento Kings]]; he had 21 points, eight rebounds, and one block in the defeat.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/dallas-mavericks/mavericks-news-kai-jones-bold-statement-nba-career|title=Mavericks' Kai Jones makes bold statement about his NBA career|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mistretta|first=Joey|date=March 4, 2025|access-date=March 4, 2025}} Jones made 12 appearances (six starts) for the Mavericks during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 11.4 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. ===Anadolu Efes (2025–present)=== On September 15, 2025, Jones signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/tr/news/GU6ZlfBqIAo8H80OYH5rag==|title=Kai Jones Anadolu Efes’te|last=|first=|date=September 15, 2025|website=|publisher=[[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]|language=En|access-date=September 15, 2025}} On February 15, 2026, Jones agreed to a two-year contract extension with the team.{{Cite web|title=Ex-NBA center signs two-year extension in Istanbul|url=https://basketnews.com/news-241259-kai-jones-contract-extension-anadolu-efes-euroleague.html|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=basketnews.com|language=en}} ==National team career== Jones was a member of the Bahamian junior national team at the 2019 [[Centrobasket]] Under-17 Championship in the [[Dominican Republic]].
